purpose: Measure the actual E1 refit and E2 retrospective calibration workload under a hard 3,000,000,000-byte memory limit with no swap and two CPU equivalents.
status: Frozen before E2 execution; E1 evaluation outcomes already examined, so E2 is retrospective development, not a new blind external confirmation.
calibration: For each previously held-out E1 experiment, fit corrections using its own early windows with target frame t+h <= cutoff. Use all eligible windows with equal weight within that experiment. Offset equals mean(target-prediction). Affine slope is max(0, centered covariance/variance), with unpenalized intercept. No hyperparameter tuning or cutoff/method selection using evaluation outcomes. If prediction variance is zero, use slope 1 and the offset correction, explicitly recorded.
evaluation: For all three cutoffs use the identical evaluation set with origin t >= 132. Its oldest feature is t-11 >= 121, strictly after every calibration target (<=120). Preserve E1 structural availability and zero-fluorescence rules. Estimate each method separately by experiment. Cells can recur in calibration and evaluation: this is temporal within-experiment adaptation, not new-cell validation. No independence-based confidence intervals.
interpretation: Prediction calibration is not a certified FD7 conditional bias bound. No direct FD7 experiment, new state-count inference, new biological observations, or power analysis is claimed. Resource pass does not imply scientific calibration success.
